business_rules.statement: The platform presents exactly five surfaces and no sixth.
No operational data originates anywhere other than the Frontline Worker Application.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Every non-Frontline creation path rejects operational-record creation

business_rules.statement: Severity classification occurs on-device at the instant of capture, including with no connection.
No artificial-intelligence component participates in deviation triggering or classification.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Trace inspection asserting no model invocation precedes a deviation trigger

business_rules.statement: No surface displays an action as applied on a device that has not acknowledged it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Command state rendering on every surface

business_rules.statement: Server-side detection atoms are the mirror and confirmation path, never the trigger.
The execution chain is implemented exactly as Job, Run, Unit Execution, Step Execution, Data Capture, with no additional level.
A Job with no runs auto-creates a single implicit run at first execution with no user ceremony.
A Workflow is linked to a Job and is never copied into it.
Job Owner is stored as a field on the Job record, defaulting to the creator and reassignable, and is not a role.
Service Type influences no runtime behaviour.
The creator of a Job cannot approve that same Job.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Job approval service in the Delivery Operations Hub

business_rules.statement: The submission passes Author, then Reviewer, then Release Authority, with the Reviewer a different person from the Author, and no role performs two stages on one submission.
JBS holds no standing access to any tenant workspace or to the console by default.
Every platform-side access to a tenant workspace occurs within one of exactly three named access classes.
Every such access mirrors into the tenant's own audit stream.
No pricing, invoicing, or payment function exists anywhere in the platform.
A tenant cannot reach another tenant's data by any route, and the control cannot be switched off by any account including the root.
The Client Command Center exposes exactly ten operational actions and no eleventh.
The Client Command Center cannot pause a run, stop a run, edit any record or configuration, create a Job or run, or override a specification or evaluation gate, for any role.
The Read-only Auditor has no Client Command Center access.
Every Command Center action executes through Delivery Operations Hub services with identical rules to the Hub's own screens.
Every capture event carries all nine envelope elements.
Exactly five command classes exist.
No capability exists anywhere on the platform for real-time remote control of a device mid-run.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Interface and application programming interface scan

business_rules.statement: The run finishes on the workflow version it started on, regardless of any republish during its life.
A Severity 2 deviation maps to a Concern and a Severity 1 to a Critical anomaly auto-entered with its containment record.
The run auto-cancel at 30 minutes applies only to unstarted runs.
No operational or administrative change commits without its audit event in the same transaction.
No interface anywhere permits altering a committed capture; corrections append.
Captured media is never written to the device gallery.
No record is deleted by age under any configuration.
No Frontline Worker Application screen in any module or state renders a pace figure, a timer against expectation, or a comparison to others.
The default Client Command Center board renders cells and lines and no individual workers.
Worker-level detail is reachable only by drill from an exception, an alert, or an approval item.
Worker-level data is held as purpose-bound aggregates, not raw behavioural feeds.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Profile memory store with personal-information-redaction policy

business_rules.statement: Anonymisation occurs at 24 months for standard commercial tenants and never in Regulated-Industry mode.
No server-side component can trigger a deviation; server-side detection is mirror and confirmation only.
The connectivity-loss protocol fires at 30, 60, and 120 minutes.
Gated work stops when the offline trust window expires; ungated work continues.
The six invariants render as locked with no off position for any account including the root.
No agent, capability, or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Evaluation gate, hard enablement gate with no off position

business_rules.statement: A worker attached to work in one calendar shift meters exactly one Worker-Shift regardless of run count.
Where a substitution occurs, each worker who actually performed work meters one.
Tier records carry no price metadata.
The burst band does not stop the floor.
An upgrade never resets consumption.
A downgrade cannot take effect mid-cycle and queues where consumption does not fit.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Tier change executed from the Super Admin platform console

business_rules.statement: Every record type has exactly one producer, matching the seam map.
Agents propose and never apply a Lane B change.
Assignment validates qualification and does not validate availability.
The audit log is append-only and is not described anywhere as tamper-evident, chained, or signed.
Timezone is anchored at Site with no Area or Shift override.
No gate is overridable by the worker it blocks.
The run_source enumeration exists with exactly the four stated values.
The inbound endpoint returns 501 at V1.
No inbound path can write an operational record.
A looser-than-floor write is rejected with the bound stated and is never accepted and logged.
Emergency pause never suppresses gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Emergency pause renders as agent unavailability, never silence

business_rules.statement: Tenants may make the platform stricter but never looser; the platform floor is fixed for everyone, always.
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing a hold, gate, qualification, approval, or command; enforcement is deterministic and local.
Every material claim carries exactly one classification from the closed set of seven.
Every permission-matrix cell in the blueprint carries an explicit status from the closed set; no cell is blank.
The drafter of a material passage is never its reviewer.
No cell in any coverage table is blank; cells that do not apply carry Not applicable followed by a specific reason.
The completeness statement states the number of open decisions and does not claim complete product coverage while any decision remains open.

decisions.question: Issue status of the Master Scope of Work version 1.2, since supersession of the five discovery documents is conditioned on issue and the status says DRAFT.
options: confirm that version 1.2 has been issued and that supersession is in force
confirm that version 1.2 is pre-issue and say so on the blueprint cover
issue version 1.2 formally as part of accepting this blueprint
decisions.impact: Two scope baselines arguably coexist until issue is confirmed.

decisions.question: Is the surface named Delivery Operations Hub (Statement of Work) or Digital Operations Hub (blueprint commission)?
options: adopt Delivery Operations Hub, matching the source
adopt Digital Operations Hub and re-issue the source
adopt one as the product name and record the other as a superseded alias
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint uses Delivery Operations Hub as authoritative and records the divergence as DEC-NAME-001
decisions.impact: Name appears in navigation, documentation, training and contracts; two names produce two glossaries.

decisions.question: How many modules does the Standards and Operations Studio have, given no canonical count exists in the source?
options: accept the derived logical model of eighteen modules from §5.1 to §5.18
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint derives a logical model of 18 modules from §5.1 to §5.18 and labels it Derived Clarification; no claim of a source-backed Studio count may be made anywhere.
decisions.impact: Studio scope may be over- or under-counted.

decisions.question: At reconnection, does capture upload or command download go first?
options: commands first (safety: a suspension, wipe or hold must land before more work)
captures first (data integrity: never risk unsynced evidence)
decisions.adopted_working_position: At reconnection stop-class commands are pulled and applied first, then every pending capture uploads with nothing discarded, then the enabling-class commands apply
decisions.status: adopted working position, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: Determines whether a suspension lands before more work is created at reconnection.

decisions.question: How long may a command remain pending, and what happens if a device never returns, for the wipe case specifically?
decisions.impact: Undefined lifetime for pending stop-class commands on a device that never returns.

decisions.question: What is the device behaviour when local storage fills?
decisions.status: open, explicitly deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification
decisions.impact: A guessed storage-full behaviour is where evidence gets silently discarded.

decisions.question: What is the membership of the set of capture types at launch, given §1.7 states seven and §5.5.3 and §7.8.3 disagree on membership?
options: the Part V (§5.5.3) wording
the §1.7 and §7.8.3 wording
decisions.adopted_working_position: Adopted on the Part V (§5.5.3) wording: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or Quick Response code scan, checkbox confirmation, digital signature, free text, and dropdown selection, plus none for instruction-only screens
decisions.impact: Determines which capture types the Frontline application and Studio must implement at launch.

decisions.question: Do Plant Manager and Quality Director exist as roles, given §3.5 says the Quality Director does not exist and both appear elsewhere as roles?
options: Plant Manager holds read-and-escalate scope only unless they also hold Quality Manager
Plant Manager and Quality Director are roles as they read elsewhere in the source
decisions.impact: Determines the role inventory and the authority of two named personas.

decisions.question: What are the floor and ceiling of the record-finish window, stated as settled in one part of the source and as open in another?
options: floor 24 hours and ceiling 7 days
decisions.adopted_working_position: ASSUM-006 works to a floor of 24 hours and a ceiling of 7 days
decisions.impact: Tenants could configure the record-finish window outside the intended bounds.

decisions.question: Does soft suspension clear on an operator signal or automatically on a payment event?
options: soft clears on an operator signal only
soft clears on a payment event fed from the client's commercial systems, requiring an inbound integration the source excludes
decisions.adopted_working_position: Soft suspension is released by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console and the platform observes no payment event, because there is no payment integration at V1
decisions.status: adopted working position, adopted 2026-08-14, open for client ratification
decisions.impact: One reading requires a payment integration the platform does not have.

decisions.question: Does worker personal-data anonymisation at 24 months stand unchanged under the no-purge model?
decisions.impact: Either identities persist longer than intended or anonymisation removes attributability wrongly.

decisions.question: Which named compliance standards mandate deletion, since deletion occurs only where a named standard requires it?
decisions.adopted_working_position: Until the list lands, no deletion path is built or promised
decisions.impact: The no-purge model's single dependency is unmet.

decisions.question: How fast must an archived record be retrievable — minutes, hours, or next business day?
decisions.impact: Blocks the audit-request-to-produced-record indicator; an audit question with no written answer.

decisions.question: What is the scope of the Custom Report Builder at V1: a formatting tool over five fixed data sets or a query surface?
options: confine the Builder to composition, filtering and saved formats over the five data sets only
extend it to arbitrary data composition, requiring Part XI to be re-opened
defer the Builder to a defined extension
decisions.adopted_working_position: Recommendation is option (a); ASSUM-022 works to composition over the five standard data sets only
decisions.status: open, newly raised by this blueprint
decisions.impact: Determines a materially different build; compounds with DEC-REPORT-001.

decisions.question: What are the identities of the five standard report data sets?
decisions.impact: Report build could start against the wrong data sets.

decisions.question: Does MES expand to Manufacturing Execution System (source usage) or Mechanical Engineering Systems (commission wording)?
options: confirm Manufacturing Execution System and Enterprise Resource Planning
confirm the commission's Mechanical Engineering Systems reading
avoid the abbreviation in all client-facing material and name systems individually
decisions.adopted_working_position: This blueprint uses Manufacturing Execution System and Enterprise Resource Planning
decisions.status: open, newly raised by this blueprint
decisions.impact: Determines which vendor category the V2 integration targets.

decisions.question: Where does an escalation go when no holder of the target role is on shift?
options: escalate to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.adopted_working_position: The platform default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.impact: Critical escalations could reach nobody; the run stays parked and is never released by timeout.

decisions.question: Is Site the mandatory minimum hierarchy level, with a default Site auto-created at tenant provisioning?
options: Site mandatory with auto-created default
Site optional
decisions.adopted_working_position: Site is the mandatory minimum hierarchy level and a default Site is auto-created at tenant provisioning — adopted 2026-08-14
decisions.status: adopted working position, awaiting client ratification
decisions.impact: If Site is optional the timezone and shift anchor needs another home.

decisions.question: Does the offline work package carry all three work-instruction difficulty levels?
decisions.adopted_working_position: The offline work package carries all three work-instruction difficulty levels until the packaging question is settled
decisions.impact: Package size, or missing difficulty levels on device.

decisions.question: Do tenant devices meet a profile sufficient for offline execution, encrypted local storage, and camera capture?
decisions.impact: Devices may not run the application as specified.

decisions.question: Is scanner hardware in tenant environments compatible with the scan capture type?
decisions.impact: Scan capture unusable at a tenant.

decisions.question: Is anything ITAR-flavoured committed to any prospect, and does a United-States-persons-only operating constraint apply?
decisions.impact: A forked deployment topology and a collision with the granted-JBS-access model.

decisions.question: When does the unit-model engineering paper land relative to the data-model appendix?
decisions.impact: The data-model appendix is blocked.

decisions.question: How are the eight platform-seeded Job Types and eight Service Type tags handled before the client names them?
options: ship the seeded catalogue empty and let every tenant create its own entries immediately
decisions.adopted_working_position: Ship the seeded catalogue empty and let every tenant create its own entries immediately; inventing names is forbidden
decisions.impact: Weakens onboarding and cross-tenant comparability until names arrive.

decisions.question: Which authority approves engineering-class capability enablement versus generic tenant feature-value changes?
decisions.impact: Blocks publishing a delegation policy for Platform Engineer and Admin.

decisions.question: Should the audit chain (write-once storage versus a verifiable audit trail) be built now given the tamper-evident deferral?
options: documented choice between write-once storage and a verifiable audit trail
decisions.status: open, a client decision, not a defect in the scope boundary
decisions.impact: AVIIXA cannot demonstrate a record was not altered, though append-only prevents alteration.

contradictions.description: The Master Scope of Work's supersession clause takes effect upon issue, but its status field says DRAFT, so two scope baselines arguably coexist.
The blueprint commission calls the surface the Digital Operations Hub; the Statement of Work says Delivery Operations Hub throughout in §1.2 and the Part IV heading.
No canonical module count exists in the source for the Standards and Operations Studio; the blueprint derives eighteen from §5.1 to §5.18.
The source never fixes whether uploads or downloads go first at reconnection; safety argues commands first, data integrity argues captures first.
§1.7 states seven capture types while the membership of the set differs between the Part V (§5.5.3) wording and the §1.7 and §7.8.3 wording.

§4.2.4 says soft suspension lifts on the operator's signal and not on a payment event, while §8.9.2 gives the exit as 'Automatic on payment' and Part IX says 'soft clears on payment'; §4.2.1 and §8.12 state there is no payment integration.
conflicting_values: release by explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console (adopted)

contradictions.description: §3.5 states the Quality Director does not exist and the Plant Manager holds read-and-escalate scope, but both appear elsewhere in the source in ways that read as roles.
conflicting_values: Plant Manager read-and-escalate only, no Quality Director
Plant Manager and Quality Director as roles

contradictions.description: The record-finish window floor and ceiling are stated as settled in one part of the source and as open in another.
§4.1.2 and §6.1.6 place a Custom Report Builder in the Client Command Center at V1, while Part XI and §4.1.5 carry report building beyond the five data sets as explicitly out of V1.
conflicting_values: report building beyond the five data sets out of V1

contradictions.description: The commission calls it the Mechanical Engineering Systems boundary; the Statement of Work writes 'the MES boundary' alongside 'ERP/MES integration' in a manufacturing-execution context.
The §4.1.5 out-of-V1 register sentence lists twenty-one phrases; the blueprint's itemisation preserves every phrase as twenty rows, and where a reader counts differently the source sentence governs.

The Delivery Operations Hub is the per-tenant operational system of record, yet no operational data originates in the Delivery Operations Hub itself — the Frontline Worker Application is the sole origin.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A source section is enumerated but not classified, or classified against the wrong locator
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The unclassified section is listed by locator in the completeness statement with the reason, and the count is reported honestly rather than rounded up
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The locator cannot be reconciled
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The row is marked disputed and treated as unmapped; the map reports lower coverage than it may actually have and never reports higher
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-read the affected Part's line range, re-enumerate, and re-issue Table A, Table B and the sub-section index together; Section 5.13 recomputed in full

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A blueprint claim carries no classification
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The assembly review flags the claim and the authoring team classifies it before issue
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The claim reaches issue unclassified
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An unclassified claim is treated by every downstream reader as Assumption — the most restrictive interpretation available — and is not buildable until confirmed
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Each issue carries a corrections list naming every claim whose classification changed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Connectivity is lost across a site
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Frontline Worker Application continues executing entirely offline against its pinned work package, classifying deviations and placing holds locally
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The outage outlasts the tenant's offline credential-trust window (default ~24 hours, ceiling 72 hours)
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work requiring an untrusted credential stops rather than proceeding on stale authority; a run blocked at a qualification gate while offline is parked and the worker continues their other assigned runs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: At reconnection stop-class commands apply first, queued captures upload, enabling commands apply last (DEC-SYNC-001 adopted position); late captures inside the record-finish window fold in flagged late_arrival

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A device never reconnects while a command is pending
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command remains queued and is applied at the next sync, in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device does not return at all
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The command remains in a pre-delivery state, rendered as such on every surface; the on-device hold was already local and did not depend on the command arriving
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Unstated — how long a command may remain pending is carried as DEC-WIPE-001 for the wipe case

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Device storage fills
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Not specified in the Statement of Work
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not specified in the Statement of Work
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Not specified — storage-full behaviour is explicitly deferred to the Frontline Functional Specification and carried as DEC-STORE-001; no behaviour is invented
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Blocked on DEC-STORE-001

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An audit write cannot commit
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None is permitted at the level of weakening the guarantee — the transaction fails, so the business action does not occur
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The failure is persistent and blocks operations
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected operation is unavailable and says so; the platform does not proceed unaudited
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Restore the audit path; an unauditable action does not happen

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant asks to delete records
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The retention horizon is shortened, which moves where data lives, never whether it exists
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant asserts a legal deletion obligation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it; the list of standards is owed by the client under DEC-DELETE-001 and until it lands no deletion path is built or promised
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Legal hold as a managed object suspends tiering and any compliance-driven deletion for its scope

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A worker is blocked at a qualification gate and no supervisor responds
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The qualification-expiry notification escalates to the Quality Manager if unacknowledged after 2 minutes
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No holder of the target role is on shift
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform default escalates to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery (DEC-NOSHIFT-001); the run stays parked and is never released by timeout
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The parked run resumes when the clearance arrives over the command channel and is applied at the device's next sync

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The worker does not start the run
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A supervisor alert fires at 15 minutes past the scheduled start
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The run is still unstarted at 30 minutes
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run auto-cancels; auto-cancel applies to unstarted runs only, so no work in progress is destroyed by a timer
failures_fallbacks.recovery: A new run is scheduled

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Consumption crosses the monthly allocation ceiling
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The escalation notification fires at 100 per cent and the burst band absorbs the overage — the floor keeps running
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Consumption exceeds 125 per cent
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant is flagged for the client's commercial conversation; the platform does not stop the floor at a threshold
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Tier upgrade, effective immediately with consumption carried forward

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Non-payment persists
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Soft suspension at 30 days blocks master-data writes while operations continue in full, with a banner to the Tenant Admin only
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Non-payment continues
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Hard suspension at 60 days makes the tenant read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline — in-flight runs complete, capture, sync, compute summaries and close; no new runs; mandatory notifications and audit continue
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Soft clears per DEC-SUSP-001 by explicit operator signal; hard is platform-initiated; archival reactivation windows 0-6, 6-12 and beyond 12 months

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A platform-side actor needs record-level operational content and no named access class is open
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Open a support session — read-only, reason-required, ticket-linked, two-hour default time box, tenant-visible banner, tenant-exercisable End-session control
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The need is a write, or the tenant is compliance-suspended
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Only the compliance-emergency path remains: named emergency class plus two authorisations (the root and one Admin), time-boxed, scope declared before it opens, automatic post-session report to the tenant. If the two authorisations are not obtainable, no access occurs
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The session closes at its time box; every access event mirrors into the tenant's own audit stream

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A second writer appears for an existing record type
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The second writer is re-pointed at the producer's service
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The second writer is a third-party integration outside the platform's control
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The integration is refused write capability and made read-only; the V1 scaffolding holds reserved external fields null and the stubbed inbound endpoint returns 501
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Field-by-field reconciliation with an audited decision per difference; no silent last-write-wins on a record type with a single named producer

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A step takes longer on the device than on paper, breaching the north star
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The author simplifies the screen in the Standards and Operations Studio and republishes through the approval chain
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The cost is a required control rather than authored excess
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The control stands and the cost is stated openly; the platform never drops a specification gate, an evaluation gate, evidence immutability, or the Severity 1 floor to win a stopwatch comparison
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The authored change is a new version; in-flight runs stay pinned to the version they started on

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant asks for a per-worker productivity dashboard or a worker-side gate override
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Met, where possible, through purpose-bound aggregates and exception-led drill, or through escalation routing
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tenant insists on crossing the non-goal
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Refused as a platform position, not a configuration option; the request becomes a platform-position change routed to the client
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Change control as a material change with client approval

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant submits a configuration value below the platform floor
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The configuration registry validates against the bound
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — there is no acceptance path
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The write is rejected outright with the bound stated; the value is never accepted and logged
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The user resubmits within bounds

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A Job is created with a unit mode that does not match how the floor tracks the work
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The worker continues on the remaining screens that do not require the unit binding, and the mismatch surfaces to the Supervisor
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Every screen in the run requires the binding
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The run does not proceed on an invented identifier; it stops and the Job's unit mode is corrected in the Delivery Operations Hub before re-assignment
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The Job is corrected, a new run is scheduled, and the partial data is preserved and excluded from the summary

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A non-negotiable is claimed but not demonstrable in the console
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The artefact is located in a different console section and the mapping is corrected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The artefact does not exist
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The claim is withdrawn rather than narrated; the non-negotiables are visible rather than claimed, so an unbacked claim is a defect
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The missing artefact enters change control as a material change

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An assumption is refuted after dependent work is built
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The dependent work is re-planned and the affected blueprint sections re-issued through change control
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The work cannot be re-planned within the programme
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The affected capability is descoped to a defined extension with an explicit record, rather than shipped against a refuted assumption
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The register is reconciled at every blueprint issue; confirmed assumptions are reclassified and dependent claims re-tagged

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A capability is absent from the in-scope versus out-of-scope matrix
